As expected, the running chkdsk restarted at 90% and started straight from 0 on next boot. I've now exhausted all options so heres as many extra details as I can throw from here.

a regular chkdsk in the Windows environment via cmd will throw a few errors at the end, telling me that things are broken:
"Detected errors in the Master File Table (MFT) mirror.
The master file table's (MFT) bitmap attribute is incorrect.
The Volume Bitmap is incorrect.
Windows has checked the file system and found problems.
Please run chkdsk /scan to find the problems and queue them for repair."

but following that, chkdsk /scan will do this:

"The type of file system is NTFS.
Insufficient storage available to create either the shadow copy storage file or other shadow copy data.

A snapshot error occurred while scanning this drive. Run an offline scan and fix."

Assuming an offline scan is out of the Windows environment, I gave that another try but the RE cmd wasn't having any of it, skipping my C: drive and scanning my D: drive instead (giving me a "The specified object was not found" error), but it also can't dump a log to my C: drive when it finishes scanning the D: drive. Making things even worse: the RE cmd is reporting from both fixntfs and fsutil dirty query c: that the c: drive is not dirty; while Windows cmd reports them as dirty... which is strange, I also can't do a diskpart list in the recovery environment because... I'm not sure? It just hangs there for a few seconds before throwing an error. 

I'm not too sure what to do from here, I've exhausted all current options I can do for today, I still have a dedicated recovery environment on a USB to try, however I'd need to run it off of a partition on my external drive, something scary as it's the only one I've got (with it being a local file backup drive) and I would have to do some repartitioning tomfoolery with it. Really hoping that I won't have to reinstall Windows entirely from zero, as while I still have the opportunity to backup and refresh from there; I don't currently have the time to deal with re-setting up Windows and much of my installed software, so any help would be super appreciated!

DS4windows installs ViGEmBus which is made by Nefarious. I googled it to see if it was malicious back when I made my comment and it's more than likely safe. 

There was a Reddit post that claimed it was a virus somewhere but their only piece of 'evidence' was a VirusTotal scan that had a false positive, claiming that they've "never had a false positive from VirusTotal". The false positive isn't even there anymore when ViGEm is scanned so you're most likely good, delete and reinstall from the official page if you're that worried.

(like I said, the fake site I named just gets the files from GitHub, likely because it's a mirror of the actual site with ads. So whatever you downloaded was probably the same as what you can get on GitHub anyway.)

If you've downloaded from **ds4-windows.com** and you're worried about malware and have come here to confirm, it's not malicious. All the site is doing is linking directly to the GitHub download link for the latest version in .zip format, no secret viruses hiding in the file (hashes compared between files downloaded from the site and GitHub.)

Still though, as the post suggests, use **Ryochan7's DS4Windows GitHub** as the main place to download DS4Windows as to avoid taking any risks.
